s1.syndrome_frame: Acute presentation of altered mental status, neurological deficits, and cardiovascular instability
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
Presented to the emergency department
Initial vital signs: blood pressure 100/73 mm Hg, heart rate 49 beats/min, respiratory rate 27 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 95% on a nonrebreather mask
Required intubation for airway protection
Computed tomography of the head showed no acute pathology
Chest radiography showed pulmonary consolidation
Electrocardiogram showed intrinsic junctional rhythm at rate of about 60 beats/min
Transcutaneous pacing delivered stimuli at about 75 beats/min
Narrow QRS complexes without visible preceding P waves

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute presentation of altered mental status, neurological deficits, and cardiovascular instability

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with altered mental status, weakness, and respiratory rate of 27 breaths/min, which are consistent with sepsis, and chest radiography showed pulmonary consolidation, suggesting a possible infectious source

shortlist.label: Myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a heart rate of 49 beats/min, and electrocardiogram showed intrinsic junctional rhythm, which could be indicative of cardiac ischemia

shortlist.label: Pulmonary embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a respiratory rate of 27 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation of 95% on a nonrebreather mask, which could suggest a pulmonary embolism, especially with the presence of pulmonary consolidation on chest radiography

shortlist.label: Status epilepticus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with altered mental status, and required intubation for airway protection, which could be indicative of status epilepticus

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with altered mental status, weakness, and slurred speech, which are consistent with ischemic stroke, although computed tomography of the head showed no acute pathology, it may be too early to rule out ischemic stroke
